quote: Are you are you, like, a subcontractor of Tesla?
stewart_read: This is the textbook Tesla expectation-gap trigger the schema flags as rare-but-real. The rep's answer at 01:49 addresses installer status but never resolves what Ion actually sells versus what the customer believes he signed up for.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately deferring full explanation to the specialist — but no bridge language ('the closer will walk through exactly what we offer') appears anywhere in the response, so this reads as an unaddressed gap, not a deferred strategy.
coaching_implication: Drill the reframe: 'Tesla referred your inquiry to us as their installer partner — we install our own panels plus the Tesla Powerwall battery, but we don't carry the Tesla roof tiles.' This single line would have closed three separate confusion touches.

quote: I was I was under the understanding that Tesla was offering, like, free free solar roofs with, battery.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same unresolved gap; rep answers with speculation about wait lists rather than clarifying Ion's actual catalog.
coaching_implication: Same fix as above — this is the second of three chances to close the gap and it's missed again, compounding customer distrust.

quote: on both ends of the yard so that they can stay south. Is that something y'all do?
stewart_read: Customer is asking a specific technical question about ground-mount configuration — an opening to redirect to the specialist and build curiosity about a custom design — but the rep answers directly with 'we actually don't do the ground mount systems anymore,' closing the door rather than opening one.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have correctly disqualified the ground-mount option procedurally — but even so, no bridge ('the specialist can look at roof placement options') follows.
coaching_implication: Coach the redirect: technical questions about mounting/configuration are closer-tier; a quick 'great question, that's exactly what our design specialist maps out' keeps momentum instead of a flat no.

quote: I don't know. I'm I'm scheduled to get a new roof with a fifty year warranty.
stewart_read: This is a direct, unambiguous roof-replacement trigger phrase. The schema's canonical response is to bridge to Ion's in-house roofing team immediately. The rep instead continues discussing roof lifespan generically.
coaching_implication: This is a lost dual-revenue opportunity (roofing sale + future solar sale). Replay this exact moment with the rep — this is the single clearest missed bridge on the call.

quote: And I'm taking down, like, eight more.
stewart_read: Tree removal improving sun exposure is a genuine enthusiasm signal — the customer is actively increasing solar viability on his own initiative. The rep briefly acknowledges but never anchors on it as forward momentum.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect this back explicitly: 'once those trees are down, your roof's going to get a lot more sun — that's worth getting an updated design on file for.' Missed opportunity to create curiosity rather than move past it.

quote: We're still covered in snow. So I don't I'm not sure when I'm gonna get my new roof. I'm definitely can't, like, think about solar until I get a new roof.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same roofing signal — customer restates the roof timing constraint even more explicitly, essentially handing the rep a second chance to bridge to the in-house roofing team. Rep's response ('you can give us a callback') just defers the whole lead rather than routing the roofing opportunity now.
coaching_implication: Two chances to say the words 'we do roofing in-house' and both are missed — this is the compounding cost of not having the bridge line loaded and ready.

quote: With the new program that we have, it is like a lease or a third party ownership program. It's guaranteed to save you money.
stewart_read: Rep is explaining financing mechanism and program structure — closer-tier content — instead of using the universal escape hatch to redirect to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be trying to keep the disengaging customer on the line by offering something concrete rather than deflecting again — a reasonable in-the-moment read given the customer had just called out the rep's lack of information. But the content given (guaranteed savings claim) is exactly what setter_scope_discipline flags as a risk.
coaching_implication: Even when a customer is pushing for numbers, the answer should stay at the redirect level: 'that's exactly what the specialist builds with real numbers for your home.' Making guarantees about savings without data is a compliance risk, not just a scope issue.

quote: It seems like you would do that first. You know what I mean? Like So that would cost you to make sure that it's feasible.
stewart_read: Customer directly challenges why no satellite/feasibility check happened before the call. Rep's answer ('For each each individual one that costs us money') is a defensive, unclear justification rather than a transparent admission or clean redirect.
coaching_implication: When challenged on process logic, a transparent one-liner ('we check interest first so we're not spending design time on homes that aren't ready — once you confirm, we run the full satellite design') lands better than an operational cost defense that invites more scrutiny.
